title: Sep 17 Results + Sep 18 Preview: Solid Ground-Ball Contact
summary: 5-4 on Wednesday with strong favorites hitting. Thursday's Top Pick breakdown inside.

content.value:
## Sep 17: Executing the Game Plan

From the mound, you learn quick—some days your best pitch gets crushed, other days a hanging curve finds the corner. Wednesday was a 5-4 performance, hitting 55.6% of our picks. Not dominant, but we got the high-leverage calls right when it mattered.

## The Breakdown: What Worked

Our highest-confidence plays delivered. The Astros (63%), Padres (61%), Rays (61%), White Sox (61%), and Angels (61%) all came through. That's the kind of command you want—when you trust your fastball, you throw it with conviction. These weren't coin flips; they were calculated reads of the matchup, and the model saw what I see from experience: exploitable weaknesses in the opposing lineups and pitching edges.

## Where We Missed

The four misses? All close-call games—Brewers (52%), Tigers (51%), Mets (50%), Reds (50%). These were essentially toss-ups, the baseball equivalent of a 2-2 count with runners on. You make your pitch and live with the result. The Brewers and Tigers were barely above 50%, and the Mets-Reds picks were dead even. That's baseball. You can't strike out every batter.

## Sep 18 Preview: Reds Host the Cubs

Thursday's top pick brings us to Cincinnati, where the Reds welcome the Cubs. The model likes Cincinnati at 50%—another tight one, but let me tell you what I'm seeing from a pitcher's perspective.

**Clay Holmes** takes the ball for Chicago. Holmes made his name as a reliever with that sinker-slider combo, generating ground balls at an elite rate. But stretched out as a starter? That's a different animal. Command becomes critical over multiple innings, and even the best relievers can lose their edge the third time through a lineup.

**Chase Burns** counters for Cincinnati. Burns has electric stuff when he's on—the kind of arm that can rack up swings and misses in bunches. The question is always consistency and how deep he can go. If he's locating early, the Cubs' lineup could be in for a long night.

content.value:
## The Pitcher's Take

This matchup screams bullpen game potential. Holmes in a starting role is still an experiment, and Burns needs to prove he can give Cincinnati length. I'm leaning Reds because of the home environment and the fact that Burns' ceiling is higher in this spot. When you're facing a converted closer, you attack early and force him to execute in high-stress counts.

It's a 50-50 game on paper, but Great American Ball Park plays differently when you know how to use it. Give me the Reds on Thursday.

**–Ace**
